jobs.title: Director of Advancement
jobs.description:
Director of Advancement

Outside The Lens | San Diego, CA
Full-time | $85,000–$93,600 annually

Help build the relationships and resources that power youth creativity.
Outside The Lens (OTL) is a San Diego-based nonprofit that creates opportunities for young people to use photography, filmmaking, and digital media to tell their stories, explore their creativity, and engage with the world around them.

Through mentorship and hands-on learning, we give young people the tools, skills, space, and support to build confidence, develop their creative practice, and make their voices heard.
We’re looking for a Director of Advancement to help us grow what’s possible. This is a senior leadership role for someone who knows how to turn relationships into lasting philanthropic support—and compelling stories into deeper engagement with a mission.

You’ll lead OTL’s contributed-revenue strategy across individual giving, foundations, corporations, government sources, and sponsorships. You’ll personally cultivate and steward key donors and funders, build a strong pipeline for future growth, and partner closely with our Executive Director, leadership team, and Board to expand OTL’s community of supporters and champions.

You’ll also lead our communications strategy, ensuring that OTL’s storytelling, messaging, brand, and donor communications work together to strengthen relationships, increase visibility, and inspire investment in our mission. This role offers significant ownership and the opportunity to help shape OTL’s next chapter.
What You’ll LeadGrow philanthropic support
Own OTL’s annual and multi-year contributed-revenue strategy and fundraising goals.
Cultivate, solicit, and steward individual donors and major-gift prospects.
Lead fundraising across foundations, corporations, government sources, and sponsorships.
Build and actively manage a strong pipeline of prospective donors and funders.
Use fundraising data and forecasting to identify opportunities and guide strategy.
Engage OTL leadership and Board members strategically to open doors and strengthen relationships.

Tell OTL’s story
Lead OTL’s communications, messaging, and brand strategy in support of our mission and advancement goals.
Strengthen our case for support by translating program impact and young people’s stories into compelling communications.
Set priorities across digital, email, website, print, media, and donor communications.
Identify the relationships, networks, events, media opportunities, and community spaces that can strengthen OTL’s visibility and reach.
Partner with the Executive Director on external engagement, relationship strategy, messaging, and follow-through.

Build a strong advancement function
Serve as OTL’s senior advancement leader and a member of the organizational leadership team.
Supervise and coach a communications/design team member and part-time grants writer.
Strengthen the systems behind the work, including CRM practices, fundraising calendars, reporting, workflows, and institutional knowledge.
Partner with Programs and Finance on impact reporting, grant management, gift reconciliation, and revenue forecasting.
Set priorities and move work forward independently while knowing when collaboration or executive involvement will create a stronger result.

What Success Looks Like
You’ll know you’re succeeding when OTL has a stronger, more sustainable advancement engine: contributed revenue is growing, relationships are deepening, opportunities are moving through a healthy pipeline, and our communications consistently reinforce why this work matters.

We’ll look for:

Progress toward annual contributed-revenue goals and a strong pipeline for future growth.
Increased donor acquisition, retention, renewal, upgrades, and major-gift cultivation.
Strong institutional and corporate funding relationships.
Reliable forecasting and consistent, on-time execution of proposals, reports, renewals, and stewardship.
Clear, focused communications that connect OTL’s impact with the audiences who can help advance it.
Strong systems and an accountable team that make excellent execution repeatable—not dependent on one person’s memory.

Your First 90 Days
Your first months will be about learning, listening, and identifying the highest-impact opportunities.

You’ll get to know OTL’s programs, people, supporters, and funding model; assess the existing advancement pipeline and systems; build relationships across the organization; and develop a focused advancement plan with clear priorities and next steps.

You’ll also establish a strong partnership with the Executive Director around donor strategy, external engagement, messaging, and relationship development.

Who We’re Looking For
You may be a strong fit if you’re a relationship-builder who also loves making things happen.
You can think strategically, but you don’t stop at strategy. You create the plan, establish priorities, make decisions, follow through, and help others do the same. You’re comfortable owning results while collaborating closely with colleagues, leadership, Board members, donors, funders, and community partners.

You bring:

Approximately 4+ years of progressively responsible experience in nonprofit advancement, development, philanthropy, or a related field, including meaningful responsibility for fundraising results.
Demonstrated success cultivating, soliciting, securing, and stewarding philanthropic support.
Experience developing fundraising strategies across multiple revenue sources.
Confidence building donor and funder relationships independently and knowing when executive involvement can strengthen an opportunity.
Excellent written and verbal communication skills, including the ability to turn organizational impact into a compelling case for support.
Strong organizational and project-management skills and a track record of following through on commitments.
Demonstrated experience developing and executing organizational communications, including areas such as content strategy, email/newsletters, digital content, storytelling, brand communications, or creative direction.
Sound judgment, initiative, curiosity, discretion, and a collaborative approach to leadership.
A genuine connection to OTL’s mission and belief in the power of youth voice, media arts, and storytelling.

Experience with major gifts, institutional fundraising, corporate partnerships, public funding, communications, or arts and youth-serving organizations is especially valuable.

And if you don’t check every box? We still encourage you to consider applying. We care deeply about demonstrated ability, potential, and alignment with our mission—not simply whether your experience follows one particular path.

Why Outside The Lens?
This is an opportunity to develop a giving program and culture of philanthropy—internally and externally. You’ll help shape a growing advancement function at an important moment for Outside The Lens, strengthening the relationships, systems, and communications that will support our next chapter.

You’ll have meaningful influence over how OTL grows its community of supporters and communicates its impact, while helping ensure that the voices, creativity, and experiences of young people remain at the center of our story.

If you’re energized by building relationships, creating opportunities, telling meaningful stories, and turning belief in a mission into sustained philanthropic support, we’d love to hear from you.
Compensation & Benefits
The salary range for this full-time Director-level position is $85,000–$93,600 annually, commensurate with relevant experience and qualifications.

Benefits include:

Medical insurance, with 100% of the employee base plan paid by OTL
Dental and vision insurance, with 50% of employee coverage paid by OTL
403(b) retirement plan
10 days of PTO annually for 0–5 years of service, with increased accrual based on tenure
Paid sick leave
15 paid holidays
Flexible work arrangements, as appropriate to the position
Professional development opportunities

Ready to Apply?
Please submit a resume and cover letter describing your interest in Outside The Lens and how your experience prepares you to lead our advancement and communications efforts. Send to hr@outsidethelens.org

Outside The Lens is an equal opportunity employer committed to creating a diverse, inclusive, and equitable workplace. We do not discriminate on the basis of any characteristic protected by applicable federal, state, or local law.

About Lifemoves

LifeMoves is the largest and most effective provider of interim housing and services for homelessness in Silicon Valley since 1987. Our Mission is to end homelessness by providing interim housing, supportive services, and building collaborative partnerships. With over two dozen interim supportive housing communities and more on the way, LifeMoves gives our neighbors experiencing homelessness a temporary place to call home while providing intensive, customized case management through site-based programs and community outreach.

POSITION PURPOSE

Reporting to the Chief Executive Officer, the Senior Director of Institutional Giving leads LifeMoves' institutional fundraising program, with a focus on private, family, and community foundation partners, playing a central role in advancing the organization's $20 million annual fundraising goal. This role carries a personal portfolio of corporate and foundation funders and prospects capable of six- and seven-figure giving, and partners deeply with LifeMoves' Corporate & Community Engagement and volunteer management team to ensure institutional and corporate-partner relationships are aligned and mutually reinforcing.

The ideal candidate is an experienced foundation fundraiser who has personally solicited and closed six- and seven-figure grants, and who brings a stewardship-first mindset to funder relationships — prioritizing deep partnership and long-term trust over one-time asks. This is not an entry-level or first-time management opportunity. LifeMoves is seeking a leader who can inspire, coach, and hold team members accountable, with demonstrated experience managing teams of 2-3 fundraising professionals.

Essential Job Responsibilities

Set and drive LifeMoves' institutional giving strategy, including prospect research, proposal and report development, and multi-year funding pipelines.
Manage and grow a personal portfolio of foundation funders and prospects, personally identifying, cultivating, soliciting, and closing gifts at the six- and seven-figure level.
Lead LifeMoves' foundation relations strategy, including prospect research, proposal and report development, and multi-year funding pipelines.

jobs.title: Managing Director, BCRF Venture Philanthropy Program
jobs.description:
About Bcrf

Breast cancer is a complex disease with no simple solution. Research is the key to stopping it in its tracks. Founded in 1993 by Evelyn H. Lauder, the Breast Cancer Research Foundation is the largest private funder of breast cancer research in the world. By investing in the best minds in science to examine every aspect of the disease from prevention to metastasis—and fostering cross-disciplinary collaboration—BCRF is accelerating the entire field and moves us closer to the answers we urgently need to be the end of breast cancer.

Since its founding in 1993, BCRF has invested more than $1 billion in research, supporting a global network of over 280 scientists across 18 countries. With annual grant disbursements reaching a record $75 million in 2026–2027, BCRF-funded investigators have contributed to the discoveries underlying multiple FDA-approved therapies and diagnostic tools that have collectively driven a 44% reduction in breast cancer deaths since 1989.

Despite this scale and impact, a persistent translational gap remains between BCRF-funded discovery science and the capital-intensive clinical development activities that carry new diagnostics and therapies to patients. Commercial venture capital has shifted decisively toward later-stage, de-risked assets, leaving pre-clinical and Phase I programs — precisely where many of BCRF's most promising discoveries sit — chronically underfunded.

To close that gap, BCRF has established the BCRF Venture Philanthropy Program (the "Program"), an evergreen investment vehicle that will deploy $100 million over five to seven years into early- and mid-stage companies advancing breast cancer therapeutics, diagnostics, and prevention technologies. The Program is modeled on the proven success of peer disease-focused venture philanthropy funds — including the Cystic Fibrosis Foundation's landmark investment in Vertex Pharmaceuticals, the Leukemia & Lymphoma Society's Therapy Acceleration Program, the JDRF T1D Fund, and the American Cancer Society's BrightEdge — while reflecting BCRF's distinctive scale, scientific network, and mission focus.

About The Role

BCRF is seeking a founding Managing Director (MD) — an exceptional individual who will build and lead the Venture Philanthropy Program from the ground up. This is a rare opportunity to shape a mission-driven investment program that will directly influence the pace of breast cancer drug, diagnostic, and prevention technology development globally, backed by the credibility and scientific network of the world's largest private funder of breast cancer research.

At $100 million, the Program is sized not merely to catalyze individual discoveries, but to reshape the early-stage breast cancer investment ecosystem. The Program will build a diversified portfolio of 20 to 30 companies over five to seven years, with BCRF moving from participant to lead investor: structuring deals, convening co-investment syndicates, and negotiating mission-protection covenants alongside leading oncology venture capital firms.

"The Program will exhibit the discipline of venture capital, and the patience and purpose of philanthropy. The Managing Director will be the embodiment of both."

The MD will serve as the Program's chief investment officer and primary operational executive, responsible for the full investment lifecycle — strategy, sourcing, scientific and business evaluation, deal structuring, Investment Committee management, portfolio oversight, and performance reporting — and will build the Program's founding team, including an Investment Principal, Operations Manager, and Associate over the course of Year 1. The MD will also serve as the Program's primary external representative to the venture capital and biopharmaceutical communities, and as a senior ambassador for BCRF's mission to donors, scientific collaborators, and the broader breast cancer community.

The ideal candidate will bring a distinctive combination of deep scientific and clinical knowledge of oncology — ideally breast cancer — and demonstrated investment experience in early-stage biotechnology. This dual expertise is the defining requirement of the role: the Program must evaluate the scientific and clinical merit of investment opportunities as its primary objective, while maintaining the financial discipline expected for a nonprofit mission program.

BCRF’s offices are in New York. While candidates based in the New York Metro area are preferred, BCRF is open to locating the Venture Philanthropy Program in the Boston, Massachusetts area and will consider exceptional candidates from the greater Boston area for this position. BCRF currently requires staff to work onsite a minimum of three days per week, and this requirement will apply to the Venture Philanthropy team.

Primary Responsibilities

Reporting to the BCRF President & Chief Executive Officer and working in close partnership with the Program's Investment Committee, the Managing Director will be accountable for the full operating lifecycle of the BCRF Venture Philanthropy Program.

Investment Strategy and Execution

Develop, refine, and implement the Program's investment strategy, ensuring consistency with BCRF's mission and the Investment Thesis.
Lead all aspects of deal sourcing, scientific and business due diligence, term sheet negotiation, investment structuring, and closing across all three investment tiers.
Build and maintain a high-quality pipeline of 100–120 annual investment opportunities, managing the funnel from initial intake through Investment Committee review and approval.
Prepare comprehensive investment memoranda and present investment recommendations to the Investment Committee.
Assume Board observer roles at portfolio companies on behalf of BCRF Ventures, LLC.
Evaluate and recommend follow-on investments in portfolio companies based on milestone achievement and evolving strategic rationale.

Scientific and Clinical Leadership

Serve as the Program's primary scientific and clinical intelligence resource, maintaining current, expert-level knowledge of the breast cancer research landscape across subtypes (TNBC, HER2+, HER2-low, HR+, inflammatory, metastatic).
Evaluate the scientific and clinical merit of investment candidates, including mechanism of action, preclinical and clinical data packages, biomarker strategies, regulatory pathway feasibility, and competitive differentiation.
Engage and manage external scientific and clinical Key Opinion Leaders who provide independent expert review during due diligence.
Maintain active relationships with BCRF's 265+ investigator network and leverage scientific intelligence from that network to identify emerging translational opportunities.

Portfolio Management

Actively monitor portfolio company progress against milestones defined in investment documentation; prepare quarterly portfolio status reports for the Investment Committee.
Provide strategic advisory support to portfolio companies on clinical development strategy, regulatory planning, partnership development, and financing.
Identify and escalate material risks in portfolio companies — scientific, clinical, regulatory, competitive, or managerial — and recommend remediation strategies.
Manage the Program's follow-on investment reserve and advise the Investment Committee on redeployment priorities.

Investment Committee and Governance

Coordinate all aspects of Investment Committee meeting preparation: agendas, investment packages, portfolio reports, and follow-on analyses; serve as IC Secretary.
Ensure the Program operates in full compliance with BCRF's governance policies, conflict-of-interest procedures, PRI legal requirements, and BCRF's broader Code of Ethics.
Support PRI qualification analysis for each investment structure.
Prepare the annual Program report to the full BCRF Board of Directors.

External Representation and Ecosystem Development

Represent BCRF and the Program at key industry and scientific conferences, including ASCO, AACR, SABCS, the JP Morgan Healthcare Conference, and BIO.
Build and maintain active relationships with life science venture capital firms, corporate VC programs, biotechnology business development leaders, academic technology transfer offices, and SBIR/STTR program officers to sustain high-quality deal flow.
Partner with BCRF's development team to integrate the Program's impact narrative into BCRF's donor communications and fundraising strategy, and represent the Program to major philanthropic supporters. Develop progress reports for the Board of Directors and key donors.

Team Building and Culture

Recruit, mentor, and develop Program staff as the portfolio grows — including the founding Investment Principal, Operations Manager, and Associate.
Build a culture of scientific excellence, investment rigor, and mission commitment within the Program team.

About You

The Managing Director will be a highly distinguished professional whose career reflects excellence at the intersection of oncology science, clinical development, and early-stage biotechnology investment. While BCRF's Program is fundamentally a scientific enterprise focused on delivering new diagnostics and therapies to breast cancer patients, it must be administered with the financial discipline expected in a nonprofit organization.

The successful candidate will most likely have built their career across two or more of the following domains: life science venture capital or corporate venture capital; pharmaceutical or biotechnology drug development; oncology clinical or translational research; or biotech business development and licensing. Candidates with a single domain of deep expertise — whether investment or science — who have not developed meaningful fluency in the other will not be considered.

In Addition, You Have The Following Qualifications And Experience

Minimum 10 years of combined experience in life science investment and/or oncology drug or diagnostic development, with at least 5 years in a senior investment role (Principal, Partner, Managing Director, or equivalent) at a life science venture capital, corporate venture capital, growth equity, or cross-over fund.
An advanced degree is required, ideally an MD, PhD and/or MBA.
Demonstrated track record of sourcing, evaluating, structuring, and closing equity investments in early-stage oncology or broader biopharmaceutical companies.
Deep scientific and clinical knowledge of oncology, with a strong preference for direct experience in breast cancer therapeutics, breast cancer diagnostics, or an adjacent solid tumor or women's health indication.
Expert-level understanding of drug and diagnostic development processes: target identification and validation, IND-enabling studies, Phase I/II clinical trial design, biomarker strategy, FDA regulatory pathways (including Breakthrough Therapy, Fast Track, Accelerated Approval), and commercialization planning.
Experience evaluating and conducting due diligence on oncology drug candidates, including critical assessment of preclinical data packages, clinical trial data, competitive landscape analysis, and IP position.
Familiarity with investment structures used in early-stage biotech: preferred equity, convertible notes, royalty-backed financing, milestone-linked instruments, and co-investment syndication.
Proven ability to build and maintain trusted relationships with biotechnology founders and management teams, venture capitalists, pharmaceutical business development executives, and academic scientists.
Excellent written and verbal communication skills, including the ability to convey complex scientific and investment concepts to non-specialist audiences including board members, major donors, patient advocates and the media.

Strongly Preferred Experience

Direct experience with breast cancer biology and/or clinical oncology — including knowledge of breast cancer molecular subtypes (HR+/HER2-, HER2+, TNBC, HER2-low), current standards of care, approved and pipeline

About LifeCampUSA

LifeCampUSA is a Christ-centered nonprofit ministry serving children who have lost a parent in military, law enforcement, or first responder service.
Through camps, mentorship, and long-term relationships, we walk alongside these young people during some of the most formative years of their lives. Our commitment does not end when camp does. We believe in showing up for the long haul.
We are a small and growing organization with national ambitions, an extraordinary mission, and stories worth telling exceptionally well.
Faith Requirement

As a Christ-centered ministry, LifeCampUSA requires all staff members to share a personal Christian faith consistent with our mission, values, and organizational bylaws.
Our faith is not a component of our brand. It is foundational to why LifeCampUSA exists and how we serve.
Role Purpose
The Director of Operations makes sure LifeCampUSA can do what it exists to do: surround children who have lost a parent in service with caring, godly mentors and life-changing experiences, again and again, without anything breaking. Every camp, start to finish. The planning, the logistics, the people who get there, the systems that hold it all together, and the safety that protects every child in our care.
This is the role that lets the ministry grow. We are building toward 15 or more camps a year, and reaching that many more children does not happen without real systems and scalable processes behind it. It happens because someone owns the operation as a whole, builds it to run at that volume, and makes sure nothing falls through the cracks when several camps are running in a season. Every system this role builds exists so more kids can get to camp, experience meaningful mentorship, and continue their journey with LifeCampUSA.
The Director owns the outcome of all operations whether or not there is a coordinator underneath them.

What You Will Own

Camp Operations & Logistics

• Own camp operations, planning, and logistics across the full season, building systems capable of supporting 10 or more camps a year.
• Own travel, lodging, ground transportation, camp gear, supplies, and the vendor relationships behind them so every camp is fully prepared before arrival.
• Own the operational systems that run the season, including CampWise, applications, forms, waivers, sessions, reports, contracts, flight tracking, camper profiles, packing lists, and season checklists.
• Own all operational pre-camp meetings and serve as the operational point of contact for camper families and mentors through the camp process, in coordination with LifeCare and the Pastoral Team.
Camp Growth & Camper Recruitment

• Identify and secure new camp opportunities and grow the number and variety of camps LifeCampUSA can offer.
• Build and manage relationships with camp locations, negotiate and sign contracts, and coordinate payments.
• Own camper recruitment and the processes that support it, including survivor coordinator and referral organization relationships, and manage rosters cleanly across program stages.
Mentor Recruitment & Readiness

• In collaboration with the LifeCare Director, own mentor recruitment and the pipeline that supports it.
• In collaboration with the LifeCare Director and Chaplain, lead mentor training and post-camp debriefs so mentors are prepared before camp and lessons are captured afterward.
Child Safety & Risk Management

• Own risk mitigation across the entire operation. This is not a side duty; it is central to the role.
• Own the child safety gate. No mentor reaches a camper without a completed background check and child safety training. This is enforced, tracked, and non-negotiable.
• Own the 3-person rule and every safeguarding protocol at camp, ensuring they are trained, understood, and followed.
• Own waivers, contracts, signed documentation, and other operational safeguards across every camp.
Systems, Finance & Continuous Improvement

• Own the operational side of camp finances, including camper deposits, travel reimbursements, camp-related payments, spend tracking, reconciliation, and reporting in coordination with bookkeeping.
• Gather camp feedback, lead operational debriefs, and turn what we learn into visible improvement season over season.
• Own post-camp reporting and summer statistics that support grants, donor reporting, and program decisions.
• Own the camp operational technology stack and build repeatable processes that allow the operation to scale without becoming more fragile.
Team & Cross-Functional Leadership

• May directly oversee a part-time Operations Coordinator and build the operations team as the organization grows.
• Collaborate with the LifeCare Director, Youth Pastor and mission coordinator on LifeCare program structure, owning the operational and systems side while pastoral leadership owns the pastoral side.
• Support key LifeCampUSA fundraising and program events where operational execution, logistics, setup, or vendor coordination are needed, while Development retains ownership of fundraising events.
• Own the operational side of merchandise in collaboration with Marketing, including sourcing, inventory, fulfillment, and distribution.

Who We Are Looking For

You are an operator who takes ownership of outcomes, not just tasks. You see what needs to happen, build the system to make it repeatable, and follow through until the work is done and the outcome is achieved.
You are comfortable holding both the big picture and the details at the same time. You can build scalable processes while still caring whether a flight was booked correctly, a waiver was signed, or a background check was completed.
You stay calm when plans change, communicate clearly, and solve problems before they become crises. When children are in our care, you understand that operational excellence and safety are inseparable.
We are particularly looking for:
• Full adherence to the bylaws, Statement of Faith, and Mission Statement of LifeCampUSA.
• Proven operations leadership, ideally in a fast-paced, multi-event or logistics-heavy environment.
• Strong systems thinking and the ability to build repeatable processes that scale.
• Comfort owning safety and compliance where the stakes are children's wellbeing.
• Experience managing people and vendors.
• Strong capability with operational tools, CRMs, spreadsheets, and camp management systems.
• Extreme ownership and a self-directed mindset. This role owns the operational outcome and does not wait to be told what needs to happen.
• A bachelor’s degree is preferred, or equivalent professional experience demonstrating the ability to lead complex operations.
• Strong comfort with technology and computer-based work. LifeCampUSA’s operations are managed through digital systems, including CampWise, Microsoft 365, spreadsheets, shared planning documents, and other technology platforms. This role requires someone who is highly comfortable working, planning, and organizing in a digital environment.
• Prior military, law enforcement, fire/EMS, or other first responder service is highly valued. Candidates from these communities may bring particularly relevant experience in operational planning, leadership, accountability, risk management, and mission-focused execution.

Compensation & Benefits

• Salary: $75,000–$90,000 annually, exempt, commensurate with experience and qualifications.
• LifeCampUSA is actively working to expand its employee benefits package, including the addition of a 403(b) retirement plan, life insurance, and other benefits. These benefits are not currently offered but are expected to be added as the organization continues to grow.

What Success Looks Like

• The operation scales. LifeCampUSA can run 10 or more camps a season and the systems get stronger under the load, not more fragile.
• Growth targets are met. New camps are identified and secured, camper recruitment fills them, and rosters are managed cleanly across program stages.
• Safety holds without exception. No mentor reaches a child without a completed background check and child safety training, and every safeguarding protocol is trained and followed.
• Every camp is fully prepared, staffed, supplied, and safe before campers arrive.
• The operation does not depend on one person. Systems are repeatable, responsibilities are clear, and the Director builds and develops the operations team as the organization grows.
• Feedback becomes improvement. Camp feedback and post-camp data drive real, visible change season over season.
• Operations works as a partner, not a silo. Development, Marketing, LifeCare, and pastoral leadership get what they need from Ops without friction.
• Leadership can trust the operation. The Executive Director does not have to worry whether camps will happen or whether they will be safe, because that certainty is what this role produces.

How to Apply

Please send your résumé and a brief note describing why you feel called to this work to:
info@LifeCampUSA.org

Applications are reviewed on a rolling basis. We will reach out to candidates whose experience, abilities, and heart align with what we are building.

The Opportunity

We are building dedicated private equity coverage for First Water Finance, and this is the seat that owns it.

Sponsors are already among our most durable relationships. We have worked across multiple portfolio companies for the same firms, deployed multiple offerings inside a single relationship, and engaged throughout the cycle from pre-close to exit. What we have not had is someone whose sole mandate is to build the relational motion, staying close enough to sponsors to maintain real visibility into their initiatives, needs, and opportunities.

You will own private equity relationships at the firm level, from deal teams and operating partners through portfolio operations and value creation groups. This is a senior, autonomous role, in direct partnership with the Founder/CEO, and the leading voice in the growth of our sponsor ecosystem.

About You

You have spent your career in and around private equity, and the sponsors you've worked with already trust you.

You may be coming from consulting, accounting, investment banking, or another professional/managed services vertical. You've likely run into the same wall more than once: the value of your relationship is capped by what you are able to bring to it, right now. So you wait and try to keep the relationship warm. This isn’t a knock on any model, it is simply a common structural limitation that keeps you from building and maximizing the relationships that you value most.

Here you would walk into every sponsor conversation with many possible entry points: assessments, managed FP&A / BPO, strategic project initiatives, and transaction support, each relevant at a different point in the hold period. When the need falls outside what we do, you can still solve it through our referral relationships across the Office of the CFO ecosystem, with the ability to participate when those connections create value. You are rarely left with nothing to offer, which means the relationships you have spent years building keep compounding rather than stalling on timing.

You thrive in environments where you can:
Develop sponsor relationships at the firm level rather than one deal or one service line at a time
Diagnose consultatively, understanding what a portfolio company actually needs before proposing anything
Be credible with a deal partner, an operating partner, and a portfolio company CFO in the same week
Operate entrepreneurially, with autonomy over how you build coverage and no provided template to follow
Stay connected to and engaged in the sponsor relationship, where interaction goes beyond engagements to knowledge sharing, content creation, and event participation

You understand that sponsors do not buy vendors. They buy people they trust to put in front of management teams, and they buy them again when the first experience holds up and the same quality and consistency can be expected. Our business and brand are built on relational strength, trust, and execution quality, which mirrors your success to date.

About First Water Finance

First Water is the Relational Finance Platform, helping emerging and mid-market businesses plot the course, make faster decisions, and maximize financing and transaction outcomes. We integrate data, FP&A, and corporate finance expertise with solutions that meet companies where they are and compound over time. Our impact shows up in the recurring dialogues that push businesses forward, and in the long-term relationships that let us step in with the right solutions when needs arise.

Our Impact:
100+ management teams and capital partners supported
10+ years of proprietary process development
$5B+ in debt and equity transactions impacted and facilitated
Repeat engagement inside the portfolios of sponsors

The First Water Finance Advantage in a Sponsor Context:

Value Across the Full Hold Period
. Assessments, FP&A business process outsourcing (BPO), project-based initiatives, and transaction support give you something relevant to bring at diligence, in the first 100 days, mid-hold for add-ons and structural change, and preparation for exit. One relationship, many entry points.
Speed to Deliverable, Consistently
. Proprietary process methodologies and internal R&D mean we deploy from experience rather than building from scratch. Functional roadmaps, reporting processes, 13-week cash flow, rolling forecasts, budgets, stood up in weeks under demanding timelines.
A Team, Not an Individual
. Fully dedicated FP&A professionals with the capacity to absorb real workload and scale involvement up or down. Sponsors have been burned by single-resource solutions and 1099 benches that are inconsistent or cannot flex with engagement needs.
Established Track Record of Execution Quality
. Answering the call in challenging, fast-paced situations, proven through long-term client relationships and repeat deployment across multiple offerings.

What You'll Do

Own the Sponsor Relationships

Activate What You Have: Bring your existing sponsor relationships into an environment that can serve them across far more situations than you have been able to address to date
Add New Firms: Develop and execute a relationship development plan for sponsors in the emerging, lower-middle, and middle market
Cover the Firm, Not the Contact: Build touch points across the sponsor organization, including deal partners, operating partners, portfolio operations and value creation teams
Show Up Where Sponsors Are: Represent First Water Finance at the events and sector gatherings where these relationships are initiated and expanded
Own the Cycle: Carry each opportunity from initial dialogue through signed engagement, then stay close as the relationship expands

Connect the Dots

Consultative Diagnosis: Get to the real problem and opportunity before proposing anything, and be honest when the answer is not us
Match to the Right Offering: Know our engagement models well enough to scope the right entry point for the situation in front of you rather than defaulting to one
Activate the Referral Network: Route needs outside our scope to trusted Office of the CFO partners, so the relationship keeps producing value in both directions
Qualify With Judgment: Pass where fit is poor, protecting both delivery quality and the sponsor relationship that produced the introduction

What You Bring

Required Experience

12+ years in business development, origination, or client relationship management, with a demonstrable track record serving private equity sponsors and their portfolio companies
An existing base of trusted sponsor relationships. This is the central requirement. We are looking for someone with current relationships at sponsors and a history of successful engagement
Background in consulting, accounting, investment banking, or a comparable professional services environment where sponsor relationships have been built over time

Industry Knowledge

Working understanding of how sponsors think about the hold period, FP&A function, value creation execution, add-on integration, and exit preparation
Fluency in FP&A and corporate finance sufficient to hold substantive conversations and connect the dots from deliverables to outcomes
Familiarity with portfolio company finance dynamics, including post-close reporting gaps, CFO transitions, thin teams, and fragmented data across acquired entities
Awareness of the broader Office of the CFO landscape and the providers operating in it

CDI is looking for an Associate Director or Director of Development to run our fundraising operations. You’ll report directly to our Co-Founder and Executive Director, who will continue to serve as CDI’s primary fundraiser. Your role will be to enable her fundraising in two key ways: (1) by running an exceptionally organized fundraising operation behind the scenes, and (2) by being responsible for grant writing and reporting responsibilities. We’re looking for a development generalist with two super strengths: (1) operational excellence and (2) exceptional writing and communication skills. You bring rigor and organization to everything you touch, and you can make complex ideas clear and compelling without flattening their nuance. We’re open to candidates with different levels of fundraising experience. You’ll personally cultivate and steward key donors and funders, build a strong pipeline for future growth, and partner closely with our Executive Director, leadership team, and Board to expand OTL’s community of supporters and champions.

You’ll also lead our communications strategy, ensuring that OTL’s storytelling, messaging, brand, and donor communications work together to strengthen relationships, increase visibility, and inspire investment in our mission. This role offers significant ownership and the opportunity to help shape OTL’s next chapter.
What You’ll LeadGrow philanthropic support
Own OTL’s annual and multi-year contributed-revenue strategy and fundraising goals.
Cultivate, solicit, and steward individual donors and major-gift prospects.
Lead fundraising across foundations, corporations, government sources, and sponsorships.
Build and actively manage a strong pipeline of prospective donors and funders.
Use fundraising data and forecasting to identify opportunities and guide strategy.
Engage OTL leadership and Board members strategically to open doors and strengthen relationships.

Tell OTL’s story

Strengthen our case for support by translating program impact and young people’s stories into compelling communications.
Set priorities across digital, email, website, print, media, and donor communications.
Identify the relationships, networks, events, media opportunities, and community spaces that can strengthen OTL’s visibility and reach.
Partner with the Executive Director on external engagement, relationship strategy, messaging, and follow-through.

Build a strong advancement function

Strengthen the systems behind the work, including CRM practices, fundraising calendars, reporting, workflows, and institutional knowledge.

Set priorities and move work forward independently while knowing when collaboration or executive involvement will create a stronger result.

What Success Looks Like

We’ll look for:

Progress toward annual contributed-revenue goals and a strong pipeline for future growth.
Increased donor acquisition, retention, renewal, upgrades, and major-gift cultivation.
Strong institutional and corporate funding relationships.
Reliable forecasting and consistent, on-time execution of proposals, reports, renewals, and stewardship.
Clear, focused communications that connect OTL’s impact with the audiences who can help advance it.
Strong systems and an accountable team that make excellent execution repeatable—not dependent on one person’s memory.

Your First 90 Days
Your first months will be about learning, listening, and identifying the highest-impact opportunities.

You’ll get to know OTL’s programs, people, supporters, and funding model; assess the existing advancement pipeline and systems; build relationships across the organization; and develop a focused advancement plan with clear priorities and next steps.

You’ll also establish a strong partnership with the Executive Director around donor strategy, external engagement, messaging, and relationship development.

Who We’re Looking For
You may be a strong fit if you’re a relationship-builder who also loves making things happen.
You can think strategically, but you don’t stop at strategy. You create the plan, establish priorities, make decisions, follow through, and help others do the same. You bring:

Demonstrated success cultivating, soliciting, securing, and stewarding philanthropic support.
Experience developing fundraising strategies across multiple revenue sources.
Confidence building donor and funder relationships independently and knowing when executive involvement can strengthen an opportunity.
Excellent written and verbal communication skills, including the ability to turn organizational impact into a compelling case for support.
Strong organizational and project-management skills and a track record of following through on commitments.
Demonstrated experience developing and executing organizational communications, including areas such as content strategy, email/newsletters, digital content, storytelling, brand communications, or creative direction.
Sound judgment, initiative, curiosity, discretion, and a collaborative approach to leadership.
A genuine connection to OTL’s mission and belief in the power of youth voice, media arts, and storytelling.

Experience with major gifts, institutional fundraising, corporate partnerships, public funding, communications, or arts and youth-serving organizations is especially valuable.

And if you don’t check every box? We still encourage you to consider applying. We care deeply about demonstrated ability, potential, and alignment with our mission—not simply whether your experience follows one particular path.

Why Outside The Lens?
This is an opportunity to develop a giving program and culture of philanthropy—internally and externally. You’ll help shape a growing advancement function at an important moment for Outside The Lens, strengthening the relationships, systems, and communications that will support our next chapter.

You’ll have meaningful influence over how OTL grows its community of supporters and communicates its impact, while helping ensure that the voices, creativity, and experiences of young people remain at the center of our story.

If you’re energized by building relationships, creating opportunities, telling meaningful stories, and turning belief in a mission into sustained philanthropic support, we’d love to hear from you.

new_jobs.title: Managing Director, BCRF Venture Philanthropy Program
new_jobs.description:
About Bcrf

Breast cancer is a complex disease with no simple solution. Research is the key to stopping it in its tracks. Founded in 1993 by Evelyn H. Lauder, the Breast Cancer Research Foundation is the largest private funder of breast cancer research in the world. By investing in the best minds in science to examine every aspect of the disease from prevention to metastasis—and fostering cross-disciplinary collaboration—BCRF is accelerating the entire field and moves us closer to the answers we urgently need to be the end of breast cancer.

Since its founding in 1993, BCRF has invested more than $1 billion in research, supporting a global network of over 280 scientists across 18 countries. With annual grant disbursements reaching a record $75 million in 2026–2027, BCRF-funded investigators have contributed to the discoveries underlying multiple FDA-approved therapies and diagnostic tools that have collectively driven a 44% reduction in breast cancer deaths since 1989.

Despite this scale and impact, a persistent translational gap remains between BCRF-funded discovery science and the capital-intensive clinical development activities that carry new diagnostics and therapies to patients. Commercial venture capital has shifted decisively toward later-stage, de-risked assets, leaving pre-clinical and Phase I programs — precisely where many of BCRF's most promising discoveries sit — chronically underfunded.

To close that gap, BCRF has established the BCRF Venture Philanthropy Program (the "Program"), an evergreen investment vehicle that will deploy $100 million over five to seven years into early- and mid-stage companies advancing breast cancer therapeutics, diagnostics, and prevention technologies. The Program is modeled on the proven success of peer disease-focused venture philanthropy funds — including the Cystic Fibrosis Foundation's landmark investment in Vertex Pharmaceuticals, the Leukemia & Lymphoma Society's Therapy Acceleration Program, the JDRF T1D Fund, and the American Cancer Society's BrightEdge — while reflecting BCRF's distinctive scale, scientific network, and mission focus.

About The Role

BCRF is seeking a founding Managing Director (MD) — an exceptional individual who will build and lead the Venture Philanthropy Program from the ground up. This is a rare opportunity to shape a mission-driven investment program that will directly influence the pace of breast cancer drug, diagnostic, and prevention technology development globally, backed by the credibility and scientific network of the world's largest private funder of breast cancer research.

At $100 million, the Program is sized not merely to catalyze individual discoveries, but to reshape the early-stage breast cancer investment ecosystem. The Program will build a diversified portfolio of 20 to 30 companies over five to seven years, with BCRF moving from participant to lead investor: structuring deals, convening co-investment syndicates, and negotiating mission-protection covenants alongside leading oncology venture capital firms.

"The Program will exhibit the discipline of venture capital, and the patience and purpose of philanthropy. The Managing Director will be the embodiment of both."

The MD will serve as the Program's chief investment officer and primary operational executive, responsible for the full investment lifecycle — strategy, sourcing, scientific and business evaluation, deal structuring, Investment Committee management, portfolio oversight, and performance reporting — and will build the Program's founding team, including an Investment Principal, Operations Manager, and Associate over the course of Year 1. The MD will also serve as the Program's primary external representative to the venture capital and biopharmaceutical communities, and as a senior ambassador for BCRF's mission to donors, scientific collaborators, and the broader breast cancer community.

The ideal candidate will bring a distinctive combination of deep scientific and clinical knowledge of oncology — ideally breast cancer — and demonstrated investment experience in early-stage biotechnology. This dual expertise is the defining requirement of the role: the Program must evaluate the scientific and clinical merit of investment opportunities as its primary objective, while maintaining the financial discipline expected for a nonprofit mission program.

BCRF’s offices are in New York. While candidates based in the New York Metro area are preferred, BCRF is open to locating the Venture Philanthropy Program in the Boston, Massachusetts area and will consider exceptional candidates from the greater Boston area for this position. BCRF currently requires staff to work onsite a minimum of three days per week, and this requirement will apply to the Venture Philanthropy team.

Primary Responsibilities

Reporting to the BCRF President & Chief Executive Officer and working in close partnership with the Program's Investment Committee, the Managing Director will be accountable for the full operating lifecycle of the BCRF Venture Philanthropy Program.

Investment Strategy and Execution

Develop, refine, and implement the Program's investment strategy, ensuring consistency with BCRF's mission and the Investment Thesis.
Lead all aspects of deal sourcing, scientific and business due diligence, term sheet negotiation, investment structuring, and closing across all three investment tiers.
Build and maintain a high-quality pipeline of 100–120 annual investment opportunities, managing the funnel from initial intake through Investment Committee review and approval.
Prepare comprehensive investment memoranda and present investment recommendations to the Investment Committee.
Assume Board observer roles at portfolio companies on behalf of BCRF Ventures, LLC.
Evaluate and recommend follow-on investments in portfolio companies based on milestone achievement and evolving strategic rationale.

Scientific and Clinical Leadership

Serve as the Program's primary scientific and clinical intelligence resource, maintaining current, expert-level knowledge of the breast cancer research landscape across subtypes (TNBC, HER2+, HER2-low, HR+, inflammatory, metastatic).
Evaluate the scientific and clinical merit of investment candidates, including mechanism of action, preclinical and clinical data packages, biomarker strategies, regulatory pathway feasibility, and competitive differentiation.
Engage and manage external scientific and clinical Key Opinion Leaders who provide independent expert review during due diligence.
Maintain active relationships with BCRF's 265+ investigator network and leverage scientific intelligence from that network to identify emerging translational opportunities.

Portfolio Management

Actively monitor portfolio company progress against milestones defined in investment documentation; prepare quarterly portfolio status reports for the Investment Committee.
Provide strategic advisory support to portfolio companies on clinical development strategy, regulatory planning, partnership development, and financing.
Identify and escalate material risks in portfolio companies — scientific, clinical, regulatory, competitive, or managerial — and recommend remediation strategies.
Manage the Program's follow-on investment reserve and advise the Investment Committee on redeployment priorities.

Investment Committee and Governance

Coordinate all aspects of Investment Committee meeting preparation: agendas, investment packages, portfolio reports, and follow-on analyses; serve as IC Secretary.
Ensure the Program operates in full compliance with BCRF's governance policies, conflict-of-interest procedures, PRI legal requirements, and BCRF's broader Code of Ethics.
Support PRI qualification analysis for each investment structure.
Prepare the annual Program report to the full BCRF Board of Directors.

External Representation and Ecosystem Development

Represent BCRF and the Program at key industry and scientific conferences, including ASCO, AACR, SABCS, the JP Morgan Healthcare Conference, and BIO.
Build and maintain active relationships with life science venture capital firms, corporate VC programs, biotechnology business development leaders, academic technology transfer offices, and SBIR/STTR program officers to sustain high-quality deal flow.
Partner with BCRF's development team to integrate the Program's impact narrative into BCRF's donor communications and fundraising strategy, and represent the Program to major philanthropic supporters. Develop progress reports for the Board of Directors and key donors.

Team Building and Culture

Recruit, mentor, and develop Program staff as the portfolio grows — including the founding Investment Principal, Operations Manager, and Associate.
Build a culture of scientific excellence, investment rigor, and mission commitment within the Program team.

About You

The Managing Director will be a highly distinguished professional whose career reflects excellence at the intersection of oncology science, clinical development, and early-stage biotechnology investment. While BCRF's Program is fundamentally a scientific enterprise focused on delivering new diagnostics and therapies to breast cancer patients, it must be administered with the financial discipline expected in a nonprofit organization.

The successful candidate will most likely have built their career across two or more of the following domains: life science venture capital or corporate venture capital; pharmaceutical or biotechnology drug development; oncology clinical or translational research; or biotech business development and licensing. Candidates with a single domain of deep expertise — whether investment or science — who have not developed meaningful fluency in the other will not be considered.

In Addition, You Have The Following Qualifications And Experience

Minimum 10 years of combined experience in life science investment and/or oncology drug or diagnostic development, with at least 5 years in a senior investment role (Principal, Partner, Managing Director, or equivalent) at a life science venture capital, corporate venture capital, growth equity, or cross-over fund.
An advanced degree is required, ideally an MD, PhD and/or MBA.

Deep scientific and clinical knowledge of oncology, with a strong preference for direct experience in breast cancer therapeutics, breast cancer diagnostics, or an adjacent solid tumor or women's health indication.
Expert-level understanding of drug and diagnostic development processes: target identification and validation, IND-enabling studies, Phase I/II clinical trial design, biomarker strategy, FDA regulatory pathways (including Breakthrough Therapy, Fast Track, Accelerated Approval), and commercialization planning.
Experience evaluating and conducting due diligence on oncology drug candidates, including critical assessment of preclinical data packages, clinical trial data, competitive landscape analysis, and IP position.
Familiarity with investment structures used in early-stage biotech: preferred equity, convertible notes, royalty-backed financing, milestone-linked instruments, and co-investment syndication.
Proven ability to build and maintain trusted relationships with biotechnology founders and management teams, venture capitalists, pharmaceutical business development executives, and academic scientists.
Excellent written and verbal communication skills, including the ability to convey complex scientific and investment concepts to non-specialist audiences including board members, major donors, patient advocates and the media.

About LifeCampUSA

LifeCampUSA is a Christ-centered nonprofit ministry serving children who have lost a parent in military, law enforcement, or first responder service.
Through camps, mentorship, and long-term relationships, we walk alongside these young people during some of the most formative years of their lives. Our commitment does not end when camp does. We believe in showing up for the long haul.
We are a small and growing organization with national ambitions, an extraordinary mission, and stories worth telling exceptionally well.
Faith Requirement

As a Christ-centered ministry, LifeCampUSA requires all staff members to share a personal Christian faith consistent with our mission, values, and organizational bylaws.
Our faith is not a component of our brand. It is foundational to why LifeCampUSA exists and how we serve.
Role Purpose
The Director of Operations makes sure LifeCampUSA can do what it exists to do: surround children who have lost a parent in service with caring, godly mentors and life-changing experiences, again and again, without anything breaking. Every camp, start to finish. The planning, the logistics, the people who get there, the systems that hold it all together, and the safety that protects every child in our care.
This is the role that lets the ministry grow. We are building toward 15 or more camps a year, and reaching that many more children does not happen without real systems and scalable processes behind it. It happens because someone owns the operation as a whole, builds it to run at that volume, and makes sure nothing falls through the cracks when several camps are running in a season. Every system this role builds exists so more kids can get to camp, experience meaningful mentorship, and continue their journey with LifeCampUSA.
The Director owns the outcome of all operations whether or not there is a coordinator underneath them.

What You Will Own

Camp Operations & Logistics

• Own camp operations, planning, and logistics across the full season, building systems capable of supporting 10 or more camps a year.
• Own travel, lodging, ground transportation, camp gear, supplies, and the vendor relationships behind them so every camp is fully prepared before arrival.
• Own the operational systems that run the season, including CampWise, applications, forms, waivers, sessions, reports, contracts, flight tracking, camper profiles, packing lists, and season checklists.
• Own all operational pre-camp meetings and serve as the operational point of contact for camper families and mentors through the camp process, in coordination with LifeCare and the Pastoral Team.
Camp Growth & Camper Recruitment

• Identify and secure new camp opportunities and grow the number and variety of camps LifeCampUSA can offer.
• Build and manage relationships with camp locations, negotiate and sign contracts, and coordinate payments.
• Own camper recruitment and the processes that support it, including survivor coordinator and referral organization relationships, and manage rosters cleanly across program stages.
Mentor Recruitment & Readiness

• In collaboration with the LifeCare Director, own mentor recruitment and the pipeline that supports it.
• In collaboration with the LifeCare Director and Chaplain, lead mentor training and post-camp debriefs so mentors are prepared before camp and lessons are captured afterward.
Child Safety & Risk Management

• Own risk mitigation across the entire operation. This is not a side duty; it is central to the role.
• Own the child safety gate. No mentor reaches a camper without a completed background check and child safety training. This is enforced, tracked, and non-negotiable.
• Own the 3-person rule and every safeguarding protocol at camp, ensuring they are trained, understood, and followed.
• Own waivers, contracts, signed documentation, and other operational safeguards across every camp.
Systems, Finance & Continuous Improvement

• Own the operational side of camp finances, including camper deposits, travel reimbursements, camp-related payments, spend tracking, reconciliation, and reporting in coordination with bookkeeping.
• Gather camp feedback, lead operational debriefs, and turn what we learn into visible improvement season over season.
• Own post-camp reporting and summer statistics that support grants, donor reporting, and program decisions.
• Own the camp operational technology stack and build repeatable processes that allow the operation to scale without becoming more fragile.
Team & Cross-Functional Leadership

• May directly oversee a part-time Operations Coordinator and build the operations team as the organization grows.
• Collaborate with the LifeCare Director, Youth Pastor and mission coordinator on LifeCare program structure, owning the operational and systems side while pastoral leadership owns the pastoral side.
• Support key LifeCampUSA fundraising and program events where operational execution, logistics, setup, or vendor coordination are needed, while Development retains ownership of fundraising events.
• Own the operational side of merchandise in collaboration with Marketing, including sourcing, inventory, fulfillment, and distribution.

Who We Are Looking For

You are an operator who takes ownership of outcomes, not just tasks. You see what needs to happen, build the system to make it repeatable, and follow through until the work is done and the outcome is achieved.
You are comfortable holding both the big picture and the details at the same time. You can build scalable processes while still caring whether a flight was booked correctly, a waiver was signed, or a background check was completed.
You stay calm when plans change, communicate clearly, and solve problems before they become crises. When children are in our care, you understand that operational excellence and safety are inseparable.
We are particularly looking for:
• Full adherence to the bylaws, Statement of Faith, and Mission Statement of LifeCampUSA.
• Proven operations leadership, ideally in a fast-paced, multi-event or logistics-heavy environment.
• Strong systems thinking and the ability to build repeatable processes that scale.
• Comfort owning safety and compliance where the stakes are children's wellbeing.
• Experience managing people and vendors.
• Strong capability with operational tools, CRMs, spreadsheets, and camp management systems.
• Extreme ownership and a self-directed mindset. This role owns the operational outcome and does not wait to be told what needs to happen.
• A bachelor’s degree is preferred, or equivalent professional experience demonstrating the ability to lead complex operations.
• Strong comfort with technology and computer-based work. LifeCampUSA’s operations are managed through digital systems, including CampWise, Microsoft 365, spreadsheets, shared planning documents, and other technology platforms. This role requires someone who is highly comfortable working, planning, and organizing in a digital environment.
• Prior military, law enforcement, fire/EMS, or other first responder service is highly valued. Candidates from these communities may bring particularly relevant experience in operational planning, leadership, accountability, risk management, and mission-focused execution.

Compensation & Benefits

• Salary: $75,000–$90,000 annually, exempt, commensurate with experience and qualifications.
• LifeCampUSA is actively working to expand its employee benefits package, including the addition of a 403(b) retirement plan, life insurance, and other benefits. These benefits are not currently offered but are expected to be added as the organization continues to grow.

What Success Looks Like

• The operation scales. LifeCampUSA can run 10 or more camps a season and the systems get stronger under the load, not more fragile.
• Growth targets are met. New camps are identified and secured, camper recruitment fills them, and rosters are managed cleanly across program stages.
• Safety holds without exception. No mentor reaches a child without a completed background check and child safety training, and every safeguarding protocol is trained and followed.
• Every camp is fully prepared, staffed, supplied, and safe before campers arrive.
• The operation does not depend on one person. Systems are repeatable, responsibilities are clear, and the Director builds and develops the operations team as the organization grows.
• Feedback becomes improvement. Camp feedback and post-camp data drive real, visible change season over season.
• Operations works as a partner, not a silo. Development, Marketing, LifeCare, and pastoral leadership get what they need from Ops without friction.
• Leadership can trust the operation. The Executive Director does not have to worry whether camps will happen or whether they will be safe, because that certainty is what this role produces.

info@LifeCampUSA.org

We are building dedicated private equity coverage for First Water Finance, and this is the seat that owns it.

Sponsors are already among our most durable relationships. We have worked across multiple portfolio companies for the same firms, deployed multiple offerings inside a single relationship, and engaged throughout the cycle from pre-close to exit. What we have not had is someone whose sole mandate is to build the relational motion, staying close enough to sponsors to maintain real visibility into their initiatives, needs, and opportunities.

You will own private equity relationships at the firm level, from deal teams and operating partners through portfolio operations and value creation groups. This is a senior, autonomous role, in direct partnership with the Founder/CEO, and the leading voice in the growth of our sponsor ecosystem.

About You

You have spent your career in and around private equity, and the sponsors you've worked with already trust you.

You may be coming from consulting, accounting, investment banking, or another professional/managed services vertical. You've likely run into the same wall more than once: the value of your relationship is capped by what you are able to bring to it, right now. So you wait and try to keep the relationship warm. This isn’t a knock on any model, it is simply a common structural limitation that keeps you from building and maximizing the relationships that you value most.

Here you would walk into every sponsor conversation with many possible entry points: assessments, managed FP&A / BPO, strategic project initiatives, and transaction support, each relevant at a different point in the hold period. When the need falls outside what we do, you can still solve it through our referral relationships across the Office of the CFO ecosystem, with the ability to participate when those connections create value. You are rarely left with nothing to offer, which means the relationships you have spent years building keep compounding rather than stalling on timing.

You thrive in environments where you can:
Develop sponsor relationships at the firm level rather than one deal or one service line at a time
Diagnose consultatively, understanding what a portfolio company actually needs before proposing anything
Be credible with a deal partner, an operating partner, and a portfolio company CFO in the same week
Operate entrepreneurially, with autonomy over how you build coverage and no provided template to follow
Stay connected to and engaged in the sponsor relationship, where interaction goes beyond engagements to knowledge sharing, content creation, and event participation

You understand that sponsors do not buy vendors. They buy people they trust to put in front of management teams, and they buy them again when the first experience holds up and the same quality and consistency can be expected. Our business and brand are built on relational strength, trust, and execution quality, which mirrors your success to date.

About First Water Finance

First Water is the Relational Finance Platform, helping emerging and mid-market businesses plot the course, make faster decisions, and maximize financing and transaction outcomes. We integrate data, FP&A, and corporate finance expertise with solutions that meet companies where they are and compound over time. Our impact shows up in the recurring dialogues that push businesses forward, and in the long-term relationships that let us step in with the right solutions when needs arise.

Our Impact:
100+ management teams and capital partners supported
10+ years of proprietary process development
$5B+ in debt and equity transactions impacted and facilitated
Repeat engagement inside the portfolios of sponsors

The First Water Finance Advantage in a Sponsor Context:

Value Across the Full Hold Period
. Assessments, FP&A business process outsourcing (BPO), project-based initiatives, and transaction support give you something relevant to bring at diligence, in the first 100 days, mid-hold for add-ons and structural change, and preparation for exit. One relationship, many entry points.
Speed to Deliverable, Consistently
. Proprietary process methodologies and internal R&D mean we deploy from experience rather than building from scratch. Functional roadmaps, reporting processes, 13-week cash flow, rolling forecasts, budgets, stood up in weeks under demanding timelines.
A Team, Not an Individual
. Fully dedicated FP&A professionals with the capacity to absorb real workload and scale involvement up or down. Sponsors have been burned by single-resource solutions and 1099 benches that are inconsistent or cannot flex with engagement needs.
Established Track Record of Execution Quality
. Answering the call in challenging, fast-paced situations, proven through long-term client relationships and repeat deployment across multiple offerings.

What You'll Do

Own the Sponsor Relationships

Activate What You Have: Bring your existing sponsor relationships into an environment that can serve them across far more situations than you have been able to address to date
Add New Firms: Develop and execute a relationship development plan for sponsors in the emerging, lower-middle, and middle market
Cover the Firm, Not the Contact: Build touch points across the sponsor organization, including deal partners, operating partners, portfolio operations and value creation teams
Show Up Where Sponsors Are: Represent First Water Finance at the events and sector gatherings where these relationships are initiated and expanded
Own the Cycle: Carry each opportunity from initial dialogue through signed engagement, then stay close as the relationship expands

Connect the Dots

Consultative Diagnosis: Get to the real problem and opportunity before proposing anything, and be honest when the answer is not us
Match to the Right Offering: Know our engagement models well enough to scope the right entry point for the situation in front of you rather than defaulting to one
Activate the Referral Network: Route needs outside our scope to trusted Office of the CFO partners, so the relationship keeps producing value in both directions
Qualify With Judgment: Pass where fit is poor, protecting both delivery quality and the sponsor relationship that produced the introduction

What You Bring

Required Experience

12+ years in business development, origination, or client relationship management, with a demonstrable track record serving private equity sponsors and their portfolio companies
An existing base of trusted sponsor relationships. This is the central requirement. We are looking for someone with current relationships at sponsors and a history of successful engagement
Background in consulting, accounting, investment banking, or a comparable professional services environment where sponsor relationships have been built over time
Proven track record of pipeline and revenue generation in a services model with long, multi-stakeholder cycles

Industry Knowledge

Working understanding of how sponsors think about the hold period, FP&A function, value creation execution, add-on integration, and exit preparation
Fluency in FP&A and corporate finance sufficient to hold substantive conversations and connect the dots from deliverables to outcomes
Familiarity with portfolio company finance dynamics, including post-close reporting gaps, CFO transitions, thin teams, and fragmented data across acquired entities
Awareness of the broader Office of the CFO landscape and the providers operating in it

Work Environment

Location: We are headquartered in Houston, TX, and our team works primarily in a hybrid/remote capacity. Our clients and capital partners are located throughout North America. Although Texas is a preference for our current event strategy, Texas is not a requirement and we will not let geography stand in the way of the right person.

Travel: Limited travel for relevant events and sponsor meetings. Schedule would be developed in collaboration with the team.

Reporting: Direct partnership with the Founder/CEO on growth planning and related BD initiatives.

Culture: Entrepreneurial, autonomous, self-directed environment where your network and expertise directly impact company trajectory.
