new_jobs.description:
Be Part of Something New. Help Transform Crisis Care.

Northern Pines Mental Health (NPMH) is bringing a new vision for crisis response to the 7E region.
After 62 years as a trusted safety-net provider of mental health care, NPMH is expanding its reach as the new crisis response provider serving Chisago, Isanti, Kanabec, Mille Lacs, and Pine counties.
Through 7E, we’re bringing proven, evidence-based models of care and building a stronger, more connected approach to responding when people need mental health support most.

This is more than a job — it’s an opportunity to help build a premier experience.
You’ll be part of a program focused on high-quality crisis care, collaboration, and creating meaningful connections between the many entities serving individuals and families throughout the region. You’ll have 24/ 7/ 365 collaborative support
when making clinical decisions and the opportunity to help shape how crisis services are delivered across 7E. With the current 7E Hub in Mora and plans to expand, you can join NPMH at the ground level of an exciting regional initiative — backed by an organization recognized as the 2026 Best Counseling Services in the Lakes Area
.

We are seeking a Program Director
to join our Region 7E Mobile Crisis Outreach (MCO)
team! This new position will be responsible for all aspects of the daily operations as well as long-term strategic development of 7E MCO within Northern Pines Mental Health Center. MCO encompasses all services provided including outreach and stabilization services. The Program Director will also function as a member of the MCO team and must be able to complete all functions of a MCO Mental Health Professional. This is a new, grant-funded role and team. The Program Director will play a critical role in developing the team, services, and community partnerships.

Essential Functions Include

Participate in 7E planning committee. In collaboration with the committee, provide recommendations for the success of the 7E team and implement deliverables
Connect with community partners to build and maintain strong referral relationships
Complete all leadership functions for 7E MCO staff including but not limited to: recruitment and selection, onboarding, training, scheduling, providing direction, delegating assignments, providing evaluations, addressing employee concerns, and addressing employee performance issues
Collaborate with Director of Operations, Clinical Director, and Human Resources to develop and enforce policies, procedures and protocols that protect the health and safety of clients and assure client needs are met
Regularly facilitate staff meetings, clinical supervision and individual supervision
Manage 7E MCO budgets including but not limited to: expenses, revenues, grant funds, and contracts
Manage daily operations of MCO programs in compliance with all state and federal regulations including but not limited to: standards of care, licensing and insurance, keeping up with and incorporating all state and federal regulations that impact applicable programs.
Maintain and monitor all contracts, grants and additional funding sources and the required reporting requirements, ensuring to meet necessary timelines.
Monitor and support individual staff’s client care goals by setting clear expectations, regularly reviewing performance, and providing coaching as needed. Clearly communicate team and individual goals, actively engage staff in their goals, encouraging a shared commitment to achieving outcomes.
Ensure appropriate documentation for clients is completed within necessary timelines, including by not limited to progress notes, evaluations, assessments, consents, treatment plans, crisis plans, and screenings.
Complete audits in collaboration with the Clinical Director to ensure program requirements are being met
Review staff documentation
Monitor and evaluate client care to ensure treatment is carried out in accordance with agency and quality standards
Complete brief crisis assessments/Interventions which will recommend inpatient psychiatric placement or incorporating crisis stabilization to assist the consumer to continue living in the least restrictive environment while maintaining their baseline level of functioning
Provide crisis assessment/intervention to consumers within the community, social services, law enforcement agencies, and emergency departments
Provide a brief risk assessment for suicidal/homicidal risk, intervention, and collaboration throughout the region, community, and emergency room settings
Develop, review, and incorporate treatment plans for crisis stabilization follow up as deemed appropriate

Qualifications Include

This position may be filled by a mental health professional independently licensed in the state of Minnesota (i.e. LICSW, LMFT, LP, Psychiatric Nurse, LPCC)
Master’s degree in behavioral health sciences
Certification to provide Board Approved Clinical Supervision in respective licensure is preferred
This role will consist of rotating day, evening, overnight, and weekend shifts
On-site presence will be required during daytime, weekday shifts.
To allow appropriate response to crisis situations, this position will include on-call hours that achieve coverage 24 hours a day/7 days per week/365 days a year
Crisis staff cover Chisago, Isanti, Kanabec, Mille Lacs, and Pine Counties, 7 days per week, 365 days per year. Primary office will be located in Mora, MN.
Travel is a function of this position; a valid driver's license is required

A wage range of $74,000 - $104,000 annually considering credentials and experience.
Health, Dental, Disability and Life insurance with other additional voluntary options for spousal life, short term disability, accident, hospital indemnity and critical illness plans
Health Savings account with employer contribution
401K with employer match
Generous paid time off (1st-3rd year 19 days/152 hours for full time then increases with longevity!)
Nine holidays observed per year as follows: New Year’s Day, Memorial Day, Independence Day, Labor Day, Thanksgiving Day, the day after Thanksgiving Day, Christmas Eve Day, Christmas Day and a Weather Float Day.
Supportive of time off for a healthy work/life balance
Bereavement Pay
Travel reimbursement

new_jobs.title: Associate Director / Director of Development
new_jobs.description:
Who We Are

The Constructive Dialogue Institute (CDI) is a non-partisan, non-profit dedicated to equipping the next generation of Americans with the skills to communicate and collaborate across lines of difference. We work with U.S. colleges and universities by providing co-curricular programming for students, professional development for faculty and staff, and strategic guidance to leadership. Our goal is to foster constructive dialogue at every level of the institution and to create the conditions for lasting organizational change. CDI was co-founded by psychologist Jonathan Haidt, the bestselling author of The Righteous Mind and The Anxious Generation .

The Role

CDI is looking for an Associate Director or Director of Development to run our fundraising operations. You’ll report directly to our Co-Founder and Executive Director, who will continue to serve as CDI’s primary fundraiser. Your role will be to enable her fundraising in two key ways: (1) by running an exceptionally organized fundraising operation behind the scenes, and (2) by being responsible for grant writing and reporting responsibilities. This role combines meaningful ownership—you’ll operate with significant autonomy—with the chance to work with an experienced fundraiser and deepen your own expertise.

We’re looking for a development generalist with two super strengths: (1) operational excellence and (2) exceptional writing and communication skills. You bring rigor and organization to everything you touch, and you can make complex ideas clear and compelling without flattening their nuance. You notice details, anticipate what’s coming, and are always looking for a smarter way to run the work.

We’re open to candidates with different levels of fundraising experience. At the Director level, you’d take on more relationship management and strategy from the start; at the Associate Director level, you’d have room to grow into those responsibilities over time. What matters most to us is that you take real pride in the quality of your work and believe deeply in CDI’s mission.

What You'll Do

Grant Writing & Management

Lead development and submission of compelling grant proposals, reports, and donor materials.
Translate CDI’s work and impact into clear, compelling narratives that resonate with funders while staying true to CDI’s voice and strategy.
Collaborate closely with Finance, Marketing & Communications, and program teams across CDI to gather the content needed for grant proposals and reports.
Maintain an exceptionally high bar for both the quality of all grant materials and the efficiency of the processes behind them.
Maintain a comprehensive grants calendar; proactively manage all deadlines for grants and other funder commitments.

Development Operations

Own the systems and infrastructure behind CDI’s fundraising work, from HubSpot and funder records to internal workflows and documentation.
Maintain and refine core assets, including reusable grant content, case studies, pitch decks, templates, and annual reports.
Partner closely with Finance to process new contributions, track grant requirements, and maintain funder and grant documentation.
Keep CDI’s fundraising pipeline current and actionable; partner with Finance to translate that pipeline into revenue projections.
Build and continuously improve the workflows, tools, and systems that keep CDI’s fundraising function running smoothly.

Fundraising Strategy & Relationships

Proactively manage the preparation and follow-through around the Executive Director’s funder relationships, enabling her to focus on relationship building.
Support the Executive Director in shaping fundraising strategy and priorities.
Conduct prospect and landscape research to identify new funding opportunities and inform fundraising strategy.
Depending on experience, directly manage and steward a portfolio of funder relationships.

Who You Are

5+ years of experience in development or fundraising, including experience writing successful grants in the six- and seven-figure range.
Passionate about development operations, with experience building systems and processes that keep fundraising work running exceptionally smoothly, particularly in smaller or growing organizations.
An excellent writer and communicator who can make complex ideas clear and compelling for different audiences.
Exceptionally organized and self-directed; you keep work moving, stay ahead of deadlines, and require minimal oversight.
Exceptionally detail-oriented, with a very high bar for quality and accuracy.
Strong judgment; you notice nuance, anticipate issues before they happen, and can assess what requires attention or escalation.
Passionate about constructive dialogue and aligned with CDI’s values.

For the Director role, we’ll also look for:

7+ years of progressively responsible experience in development or fundraising, including 2+ years in management or leadership roles.
Experience owning funder relationships through cultivation, solicitation, and stewardship.
Experience building and executing fundraising strategies to achieve philanthropic revenue goals of $1 million or more.

What We Offer

A Mission-Driven Culture
— our work culture genuinely reflects our mission, characterized by intellectual humility, continuous improvement, and open-mindedness
Unlimited PTO
— recharge on your own schedule with unlimited paid time off, in addition to 13 company holidays
Health, Vision & Dental
— health, vision, and dental plans through, with CDI contributing toward your premiums each month
401(k) Match
— invest in your future with a 100% match on your contributions, up to 3% of your pay
Professional Development
— an annual budget to invest in your growth: build new skills, deepen existing ones, and stay inspired in your work
Remote Work Support
— up to $500 reimbursed for home office equipment and up to $50/month reimbursed for home internet or cell phone expenses

The Details

Compensation: Associate Director: $101,000–$113,000; Director: $132,000–$147,000

Reports to
: Executive Director
Direct reports: None

Schedule:
Full-time, flexible within U.S. time zones
Target start date: ASAP

Location:
Remote, must be based in the U.S.

We know AI has become a useful writing assistant, and we’re comfortable with candidates using it that way. But when AI does too much of the writing, applications start to sound remarkably similar, making it hard for us to understand what you uniquely bring to the table. Please keep this in mind as you prepare your application.
